_note: Real ML Kit line output for a single-column card whose text sizes span a factor of eight, captured 2026-09-03. The logo is 448 pixels tall and the strapline beneath it 74.
_anonymised: Boxes are exactly as ML Kit reported them, converted from the captured centre-y and height. The person's name, the company name, the email and the telephone numbers are replaced by strings of the same shape - same word counts, character classes, lengths and OCR damage, including the pipe the recogniser read for a '1' in the second number and the single letter it got wrong in the email against the printed name. The city and country are left as printed.
_source: Samsung SM-G736B, ML Kit text-recognition, Latin. Line angles between -0.9 and +1.5 degrees.
_layout: One column, centred, top to bottom: a very large logo, a small strapline, the name, the title, two telephones, the email, then two address lines.
_why_it_matters: Line heights run 52 to 448 on one card. Every rule that measures in line heights - the gap test, the name-is-the-largest-text rule - is being asked to hold across an eight-fold range on a single card, and the logo is by far the largest text on it.
